title: Polygons
examples: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
If a polygon has 7 sides, what is the sum of its exterior angles?
How do I find the number of sides if I know the exterior angle?

explain.say: Today we are learning about polygons and their angles. A polygon is a closed shape made of straight lines. Think about a triangle or a square. These are all examples of polygons.
The sum of the interior angles of any polygon with n sides is given by the formula (n minus two) times 180 degrees. For example, a quadrilateral has 4 sides, so the sum is two times 180 degrees.
Next, we look at the exterior angles. No matter how many sides the polygon has, the sum of all its exterior angles always equals 360 degrees. This is a very useful rule to remember.

If a polygon is regular, all its sides and all its angles are equal. To find one exterior angle, you just divide 360 degrees by the number of sides. For example, a regular pentagon has an exterior angle of 72 degrees.

faq.q: What is the difference between interior and exterior angles?
faq.a: The interior angle is the angle inside the polygon. The exterior angle is the angle formed by one side and the extension of an adjacent side.
asks: What are interior and exterior angles?

faq.q: Does the sum of exterior angles change for different polygons?
faq.a: No, the sum of the exterior angles is always 360 degrees, regardless of how many sides the polygon has. This is a constant rule.
asks: Is the exterior angle sum always 360?
What is the total of exterior angles?

faq.q: How do I find the number of sides if I know one exterior angle?
faq.a: You can divide 360 degrees by the measure of that single exterior angle. This will give you the number of sides, or n.
asks: If the exterior angle is 30 degrees, how many sides does it have?
What is n if the exterior angle is 36 degrees?

faq.q: Does this formula work for non-regular polygons too?
faq.a: The sum formulas for both interior and exterior angles work for all simple polygons, regular or not. The 'regular' part only means all angles are equal.
asks: Do I need it to be regular for the angle sums?
Can I use the formulas on an irregular shape?

faq.a: A regular polygon is a polygon where all sides are equal in length and all interior angles are equal in measure. Think of a perfect square.
asks: Are all sides and angles the same in a regular polygon?

facts: The sum of the interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n minus two) times 180 degrees.
The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon is always 360 degrees.
In a regular polygon, all interior angles are equal, and all exterior angles are equal.
To find one exterior angle of a regular polygon, divide 360 degrees by the number of sides.
